32: KHLESTAKOV. Very well. About a loan I won't say a word. I'll take it.
30: MERCHANTS. If you please, father. [They take out money.] But what is three hundred? Better take five hundred. Only help us.
28: KHLESTAKOV. No, no. Don't think of it. I don't take bribes. Oh, if, for example, you would offer me a loan of three hundred rubles, that's quite different. I am willing to take a loan.
26: MERCHANTS. It doesn't matter where you are pleased to send him. Only the farthest away from here the better. Father, don't scorn to accept our bread and salt. We pay our respects to you with sugar and a basket of wine.
24: KHLESTAKOV. What a swindler! For such things a man can be sent to Siberia.
22: MERCHANTS. Yes, indeed! And try to contradict him, and he'll fill your house with a whole regiment of soldiers. And if you say anything, he orders the doors closed. "I won't inflict corporal punishment on you," he says, "or put you in the rack. That's forbidden by law," he says. "But I'll make you swallow salt herring, my good man."
21: KHLESTAKOV. Why, he's a plain robber.
19: MERCHANTS. So help us God! No one remembers a governor like him. When you see him coming you hide everything in the shop. It isn't only that he wants a few delicacies and fineries. He takes every bit of trash, too—prunes that have been in the barrel seven years and that even the boy in my shop would not eat, and he grabs a fist full. His name day is St. Anthony's, and you'd think there's nothing else left in the world to bring him and that he doesn't want any more. But no, you must give him more. He says St. Onufry's is also his name day. What's to be done? You have to take things to him on St. Onufry's day, too.
17: KHLESTAKOV. Is it possible? My, what a swindler!
14: MERCHANTS. Don't ruin us, your Worship. We suffer insult and wrong wholly without cause.
10: Khlestakov and Merchants, with a basket of wine and sugar loaves. KHLESTAKOV. What is it, friends?
8: KHLESTAKOV [takes the petitions through the window, unfolds one of them and reads]. "To his most honorable, illustrious financial Excellency, from the merchant Abdulin...." The devil knows what this is! There's no such title.
7: KHLESTAKOV. Let them in, let them in. Osip, tell them to come in. Osip goes out.
5: MERCHANT'S VOICE. We appeal for your protection. Give orders, your Lordship, that our petitions be received.
4: KHLESTAKOV [going to the window]. What is it, friends?
2: OSIP [looking through the window]. There are some merchants there who want to come in, and the sergeant won't let them. They are waving papers. I suppose they want to see you.
1: KHLESTAKOV. What's the matter there, Osip? See what the noise is about.
